title: Storage Box
description: A storage box is an open-top pine box 24 inches long for books, tools, or toys, with a plywood bottom set onto cleats and two handle cleats on the short sides for carrying. Butt joints and screws build it in an afternoon, and the bottom cleats, rather than nails alone, carry the weight so a loaded box does not drop its bottom. Boxes stack when their sides are kept square, and labels on the short side keep a stack readable.

title: Crate
description: A crate is a slatted open box for produce, records, or firewood kindling, built from thin pine slats over four corner posts with gaps between the slats for air and handholds. The gaps keep produce ventilated and let a hand grip any side, and the corner posts carry the stacking weight so a stack of crates does not crush the lowest one. It is the cheapest storage build in the pair and the best practice for square assembly, because a crate that is not square will not stack.

title: Shoe Rack

title: Under-Bed Box
description: An under-bed box is a low rolling box 7 inches high that slides under a bed for blankets and out-of-season clothes. It is built from half-inch plywood to save height, rides on four small casters so it rolls out without lifting, and has a finger pull on its front face instead of a handle that would snag bedding. The low height is the whole design problem: every joint is kept flush and the casters are counted in the 7 inch total, so the box clears the bed frame.

title: Blanket Chest
description: A blanket chest is a cedar-lined chest 49 inches long overall that sits at the foot of a bed for blankets and quilts, and cedar is chosen for its moth-discouraging scent and its resistance to damp. The chest is built like the storage chest but wider and lower, with feet that lift it off the floor, a lid on stays, and an inside left unfinished or clear-finished so blankets never pick up paint smell. It doubles as a bench for sitting to put shoes on, but it is never a step for reaching high places.

title: Garage Shelving
description: Garage shelving is a heavy freestanding unit 96 inches wide and 72 inches high for bins, tools, and paint, built from two-by-four uprights and long shelf beams. The span is broken by a middle upright pair so no shelf beam spans more than 48 inches under load, back braces keep it square, and a wall strap anchors it, because a garage unit is loaded unevenly and bumped by cars and doors. Shelf boards run front to back in groups so a single damaged board can be replaced without rebuilding a shelf.

title: Wardrobe
description: A wardrobe is a tall clothes cabinet 48 inches wide and 72 inches high, with two doors, a hanging rail for coats and shirts, and two shelves for folded clothes. The case is built square and strapped to the wall before loading, because a wardrobe full of clothes is top-heavy and can tip. Doors are hung last, after the case is level, with two hinges each and magnetic catches, and the hanging rail is fixed into the sides with brackets rated for a full rail of winter coats. Ventilation comes from a small gap under the doors so stored clothes do not smell musty.
